help.intro: A radio interview of about one and a half minutes with a baker: he gets up at three in the morning, bakes four hundred rolls before you wake up, and has his evening at six. He explains why the bread tastes different in every town, what the hardest hour of his day is and why there are fewer and fewer bakeries like his. The baker is an invented person; the working hours and the numbers are the real ones of the trade. You hear what you have just learnt: times (um drei Uhr, um halb vier, von vier bis acht), separable verbs in a day's routine (aufstehen, anfangen, aufmachen, zumachen, einschlafen) and the connectors und, aber, dann, deshalb that join his sentences. Listen once for the whole day, then once for each time.
help.tips[0].title: The day in times and separable verbs
help.tips[0].text: Um drei Uhr stehe ich auf (aufstehen). Um halb vier fange ich an (anfangen). Um sechs machen wir auf (aufmachen = to open). Um achtzehn Uhr machen wir zu (zumachen = to close). Um neun schlafe ich ein (einschlafen). The prefix goes to the end; the time usually comes first and pushes the verb into position 2: Um drei Uhr stehe ich auf. Clock times: halb vier = 3:30, Viertel nach vier = 4:15, Viertel vor fünf = 4:45.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: At three o'clock I get up, at half past three I start.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: At six we open the shop, at six in the evening we close.
help.tips[0].check.why: halb vier = half of the way to four = 3:30.
help.tips[1].title: Joining sentences: und, aber, dann, deshalb
help.tips[1].text: und (and) and aber (but) join two sentences without changing the word order: Ich stehe früh auf, aber ich bin nicht müde. dann (then) and deshalb (that is why) take position 1 and push the verb to position 2: Dann fange ich an. Deshalb gibt es weniger Bäckereien. Also zuerst (first), danach (after that), später (later) work like dann.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: First I switch on the oven, then I knead the dough, after that I shape the rolls.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The work is hard, that is why we hardly find apprentices.
help.tips[1].check.q: Ich bin müde, ____ gehe ich früh ins Bett.
help.tips[1].check.why: deshalb = that is why; it gives the consequence and takes position 1 with the verb right after it.
help.remember[0]: Um drei Uhr stehe ich auf; um sechs machen wir auf; um achtzehn Uhr machen wir zu.
help.remember[1]: und / aber keep the word order; dann / deshalb / danach take position 1, verb in position 2.
help.exam: Short interviews about a person's day with times and routines are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Three in the morning, four hundred rolls before sunrise, and bed at nine: listen to a baker's day, hour by hour.
passageTranslation:
Reporter: Mr Lang, you are a baker in Bamberg. When does your day begin?
Baker: At three o'clock. That is when the alarm rings. At half past three I am in the bakehouse and start.
Reporter: What do you do first?
Baker: First I switch on the oven. Then I knead the dough for the rolls. After that I shape the rolls, about four hundred. At five o'clock the first loaves go into the oven.
Reporter: And when do you open the shop?
Baker: At six o'clock. My wife opens the shop, and I keep baking. From six to eight it is very busy. Everyone wants fresh rolls for breakfast.
Reporter: What is the hardest hour?
Baker: The first. Getting up at three is hard, even after thirty years. But then it is quiet in the bakehouse, only me and the oven. I like that.
Reporter: Why does your bread taste different from the bread in the supermarket?
Baker: The dough needs time. My dough rests twelve hours, in the supermarket often only one. And every town has its own recipe. That is why the bread in Bamberg tastes different from Hamburg.
Reporter: How many bakeries are there still in Germany?
Baker: About nine thousand. Thirty years ago there were twice as many. The work is hard and the night is long, that is why we hardly find young people.
Reporter: And when does your day end?
Baker: At one o'clock I am finished baking. Then I sleep for two hours. At six in the evening we close the shop, we eat together, and at nine I fall asleep. At three the alarm rings again.
questions[0].explanation: "Um drei Uhr. Da klingelt der Wecker." At half past three he starts work.
questions[0].questionTranslation: At what time does the baker get up?
questions[1].explanation: "Zuerst mache ich den Ofen an. Dann knete ich den Teig …"
questions[1].questionTranslation: What does he do first in the bakehouse?
questions[2].explanation: "Danach forme ich die Brötchen, etwa vierhundert Stück."
questions[2].questionTranslation: How many rolls does he shape?
questions[3].explanation: auf … machen = aufmachen (to open); the prefix auf stands at the end.
questions[3].questionTranslation: 'At six o'clock. My wife opens the shop.' Which verb is that?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: zumachen, separable: to close the shop in the evening
questions[4].explanation: "Von sechs bis acht ist es sehr voll. Alle wollen frische Brötchen zum Frühstück."
questions[4].questionTranslation: When is the shop very busy?
questions[4].optionsTranslation[0]: from three to five in the morning
questions[5].options[1]: weil sein Teig zwölf Stunden ruht und jede Stadt ihr eigenes Rezept hat
questions[5].explanation: "Mein Teig ruht zwölf Stunden, im Supermarkt oft nur eine. Und jede Stadt hat ihr eigenes Rezept."
questions[5].questionTranslation: Why does his bread taste different from the supermarket?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: because his dough rests twelve hours and every town has its own recipe
questions[5].optionsTranslation[2]: because he gets up at three and bakes the first loaves at five already
questions[6].explanation: deshalb = that is why; it introduces the consequence of the hard work and takes position 1, verb in position 2 (finden wir).
questions[6].questionTranslation: 'The work is hard and the night is long, that is why we hardly find young people.' What does deshalb show?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[0]: a contrast between the work and the night
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: the consequence: that is why there are hardly any young people
questions[7].explanation: "… und um neun Uhr schlafe ich ein. Um drei Uhr klingelt wieder der Wecker."
questions[7].questionTranslation: When does the baker fall asleep?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: at six in the evening, right after the shop
questions[3].options[2]: zumachen, trennbar: den Laden am Abend schließen
questions[5].options[2]: weil er um drei Uhr aufsteht und schon um fünf Uhr die ersten Brote backt
